hook: *₹36 crore* saved: TGSRTC buses now grade how drivers drive
hook_b: *₹36 crore* saved: TGSRTC buses now grade how drivers drive
tldr: TGSRTC says the i-ALERT system in 1,500 BS-VI buses has saved nearly ₹36 crore in diesel, about ₹2 crore a month.

beats.what: The i-ALERT system in 1,500 Ashok Leyland BS-VI buses saves about 1.98 lakh litres of diesel a month, TGSRTC MD Anil Kumar said.
beats.why: It tracks gear use, engine RPM, idling, overspeeding and harsh braking, and grades each driver after every shift.
beats.care: TGSRTC says it is the first state transport corporation to use the system; APSRTC and KSRTC have asked for details.

effects.label: Other states asking to copy it

cards.title: 🆕 What's new
cards.body: Drivers get individual performance reports and feedback after each shift to keep the engine in the 'Green Band' RPM range.

cards.q: How do TGSRTC bus rides feel to you lately?

qs: Will the system reach older, non-BS-VI buses too?
Does grading drivers change how passengers experience rides?

facts.t: The system runs in *1,500* Ashok Leyland BS-VI buses.
TGSRTC estimates *6,169.84 tonnes* of CO2 avoided a year.

viz.verdict: Less diesel burnt means fewer emissions from city buses

watch: APSRTC and KSRTC officials have sought details on how the system performs.
